canonical_name: THE DEPTH: the Energy Blueprint, the Domains By-year lines, and the round-8 golden units of the in-depth sections
construct: Station-only (owner rulings 2026-10-17/18 A1–W15, B1–B4; R2 A 2026-10-21): every unit keyed as depthResolve.js reads it. Slot templates ({god} {element} {count} {holder} {when} {a} {b} {share} {a_noun} {b_noun} {breakers} {stand} {gods}) are filled by the resolver. The chapter and star keys here are the round-8 golden units; Life Chapters and Stars supersede them with their own modules.
candidate_note: Golden units approved in round 8 (https://claude.ai/artifact/J5JMZEioCtMy3x7dadZkVN); batches adopted through the depth gate.

units.GOD bijian · missing: Going it alone is never your first move. With a team or a close friend beside you, you find your footing faster and hold it longer.
units.GOD bijian · season_need.hidden: You hold the Twin only as a trace in the depths of a branch, a thin seam of your own element that keeps a heavy season from outweighing you.
units.GOD bijian · season_need.rooted: Your own element runs through one branch as its main stem, and the Twin there braces you against a season that gives you little of it.
units.GOD bijian · season_need.shown: You hold the Twin in plain view on a stem, where it adds more of your own element to a season that runs short of it.
units.GOD bijian · seen.inside: In private you want to answer to nobody and would rather finish a job alone than wait for a hand.
units.GOD bijian · seen.plain: You come across as someone who carries their own weight and asks for little help.
units.GOD bijian · year_domain.Family: With siblings and cousins weighing in, you settle family matters this year between equals of your own age.
units.GOD bijian · year_domain.Growth: This year you see your own shape by working alongside equals, leaning less on anyone's approval and more on your own judgement.
units.GOD bijian · year_domain.Social: Among friends this year, you spend more time with peers who do what you do than with anyone who looks up to you.
units.GOD bijian · year_line.heavy: Your life fills with equals, a new colleague or a friend who wants exactly what you want. You compete more than you admit, and you come out of it more set in your own way.
units.GOD jiecai · missing: Winning for its own sake leaves you cold, and you rarely line yourself up against friends. When a colleague wants the same post, you find out how much you want it.
units.GOD jiecai · season_need.hidden: Your chart buries the Rival in the lowest layer of a branch, a sliver of your element's other half that still answers a season with almost none.
units.GOD jiecai · season_need.rooted: You hold the Rival as the chief stem inside a branch, where it banks your element in its second form for a season that comes up short.
units.GOD jiecai · season_need.shown: Your chart sets the Rival on a stem for anyone to see, bringing your own element in its other form to a season that leans against you.
units.GOD jiecai · seen.inside: You keep score with the people closest to you, and you want to win more than you let on.
units.GOD jiecai · seen.plain: To most people you look bold and openhanded, quick to share what you have and quicker to race for more.
units.GOD jiecai · year_domain.Career: You keep your share this year by naming it before anyone else does, as a colleague or partner reaches for the same credit.
units.GOD jiecai · year_domain.Social: This year you compete with friends for the same invitations and attention, sharing your circle more widely than you planned.
units.GOD jiecai · year_domain.Wealth: You decide how much of your own goes in this year, as shared purchases and a friend's request for help pull at your money.
units.GOD jiecai · year_line.heavy: Someone arrives who wants a share of what you have, at work or among friends. You give ground on money or credit before you notice, and you hold the rest only by being blunt.
units.GOD piancai · chapter_decade.helping.com: This decade opens side roads and second ventures, and you find money and company in places you had never looked.
units.GOD piancai · missing: Offers you did not chase seldom find you, and side doors stay shut until you knock. You earn by the front route, one job at a time, trusting what you worked for over a windfall.
units.GOD piancai · season_need.hidden: Your chart holds the Horizon only far down in one branch, a small field where your strength can range in a season that brings hardly any.
units.GOD piancai · season_need.rooted: You hold the Horizon at the heart of a branch, where its element slips in by a side door and gives a lean season something to work on.
units.GOD piancai · season_need.shown: You keep the Horizon in full view, where its element opens a wide field for your strength in a season that offers it little to work.
units.GOD piancai · seen.inside: You keep a second plan that nobody has heard about and want more open roads than you admit.
units.GOD piancai · seen.plain: In company you are easy with newcomers and quick with an offer, the one who always knows someone useful.
units.GOD piancai · year_domain.Family: Your family life widens this year to relatives far away or newly met, drawing your time and money to people beyond your own door.
units.GOD piancai · year_domain.Social: You move easily this year between groups that never meet each other, carried there by chance meetings and introductions.
units.GOD piancai · year_domain.Wealth: Through a second job or an unexpected offer, you take in money by side doors this year and spread it across more ventures than usual.
units.GOD pianyin · chapter_decade.heavy.lived: These years kept you studying and second-guessing longer than your friends, and you came out of them knowing more than you could yet use.
units.GOD pianyin · missing: Odd subjects and second thoughts rarely pull at you. You take knowledge as it is taught and act on a straight answer before you think to question it.
units.GOD pianyin · season_need.hidden: Far beneath the surface, you hold the Alchemist as a thin thread, a trickle of its element feeding you where the season gives nothing.
units.GOD pianyin · season_need.rooted: Underneath, you carry the Alchemist as a branch's main stem, and its element feeds you by a back route your season does not offer.
units.GOD pianyin · season_need.shown: On a stem in open view, you have the Alchemist feeding your element by an unusual route, the supply your season fails to give.
units.GOD pianyin · seen.inside: You think in strange directions and keep most of those thoughts to yourself.
units.GOD pianyin · seen.plain: From the outside you look unusual and hard to read, with a specialist interest nobody saw coming.
units.GOD pianyin · year_domain.Career: This year you learn more out of sight than you earn in plain view, with your work turned toward study and specialist skill.
units.GOD pianyin · year_domain.Growth: Out of public view, you grow more yourself this year through solitary study and interests nobody assigned you.
units.GOD pianyin · year_domain.Mind: You study alone this year, pulled toward odd, specialist subjects nobody nearby would think to ask about.
units.GOD pianyin · year_line.heavy: Your attention turns inward, toward study and second thoughts and plans you keep to yourself. You get less done than you meant to, and you understand more at the end than at the start.

units.GOD qisha · seen.plain: You read as tough and hard to rattle, the person people send in when the stakes are high.
units.GOD qisha · year_domain.Career: You hold up better than anyone expects this year, when a demanding task or a rival with standing tests your work.

units.GOD qisha · year_domain.Health: Pressure settles into your body this year as tension you carry without noticing, and you feel it first in your sleep.
units.GOD qisha · year_line.helping: A hard test arrives from outside, a demanding boss or a rival or a deadline you did not set. You meet it better than you expect, and people remember how you handled it.
units.GOD shangguan · chapter_decade.helping.c: This decade gives your voice back its edge, and you say what you think with more freedom than you allowed yourself before.
units.GOD shangguan · missing: Arguing back is not your first reflex when a plan looks wrong. You follow the brief as written and raise objections late and politely, after the decision is made.
units.GOD shangguan · season_need.hidden: You keep the Virtuoso as a minor stem at the bottom of a branch, a faint vent for force that a closed season would otherwise trap.
units.GOD shangguan · season_need.rooted: You carry the Virtuoso as the ruling stem of a branch, its element venting force that builds up in a season with no such release.
units.GOD shangguan · season_need.shown: You carry the Virtuoso openly on a stem, and its element cuts a channel for the force your season keeps pent up in you.
units.GOD shangguan · seen.inside: You rewrite other people's work in your head and want your talent noticed without having to point to it.
units.GOD shangguan · seen.plain: You strike people as quick and outspoken, the one who says what the rest of the meeting was thinking.
units.GOD shangguan · year_domain.Career: Sure of your skill and short with the rules, you say out loud this year what colleagues only grumble about.
units.GOD shangguan · year_domain.Mind: Your thinking sharpens against the ideas you are handed this year, finding flaws in what others accept faster than you can keep quiet about them.
units.GOD shangguan · year_domain.Social: Your conversations with friends grow sharper and wittier this year, until you are the one your circle quotes the next day.

units.GOD shishen · season_need.hidden: With the Artisan only deep in a branch, you have a narrow outlet, enough to let some stored force out into a season that would hold it in.
units.GOD shishen · season_need.rooted: Your chart keeps the Artisan as the main stem within a branch, a hidden outlet that turns stored force into something made where the season offers none.
units.GOD shishen · season_need.shown: With the Artisan on show, you send your strength out through its element, an outlet that a season short of it never opens for you.
units.GOD shishen · seen.inside: You want comfort more than you show, good food and an evening with nothing planned.
units.GOD shishen · seen.plain: You seem easygoing and warm, the friend who cooks for everyone and makes hard work look light.
units.GOD shishen · year_domain.Career: You get paid more readily this year for what you enjoy making, because your work loosens and pleases people.
units.GOD shishen · year_domain.Family: This year you cook, host and make the place feel lived in, with home gathering around food and easy company.
units.GOD shishen · year_domain.Health: Your body follows the pace you set this year, with meals, sleep and easy pleasures filling more of your days.
units.GOD shishen · year_line.helping: Your appetite comes back, for good food and for the work you enjoy making. Your work gets easier and better liked, and you finish with something you made that people keep.
units.GOD zhengcai · chapter_decade.helping.co: This decade rewards patience with steady returns, and you build the kind of security that lets you stop counting.
units.GOD zhengcai · missing: You do the books when you must and not a day sooner. You handle money in bursts and forget it for months, leaning on a partner or a spreadsheet to keep track.
units.GOD zhengcai · season_need.hidden: What you hold of the Steward lies deep in a branch, a small, solid store for your strength to work when the season supplies next to nothing.
units.GOD zhengcai · season_need.rooted: You keep the Steward as the leading stem of a branch, out of sight, a steady store of material for a season that has little to give.
units.GOD zhengcai · season_need.shown: Your chart puts the Steward right on the surface, where its element gives your strength something solid to shape in a season with little to hold.

units.GOD zhengcai · seen.plain: You come across as a careful provider, the one who pays on time and keeps count.

units.GOD zhengcai · year_domain.Family: You keep the household accounts this year and see to family property, holding the home in careful order.
units.GOD zhengcai · year_domain.Wealth: Your attention turns to bills, savings and the slow work of keeping accounts this year, until you know where each part of your money goes.

units.GOD zhengguan · missing: You look to others to learn what the rules are. You borrow structure from a boss or a contract, and you work best once someone else has fixed the terms.
units.GOD zhengguan · season_need.hidden: Your chart tucks the Magistrate into one deep corner of a branch, a slight check from its element that gives a formless season some measure.

units.GOD zhengguan · seen.plain: You present as reliable and correct, the person others trust to follow the rules and keep their word.

units.GOD zhengguan · year_domain.Family: You carry family duties in full view of your relatives this year, from the paperwork and signatures to speaking for the household.
units.GOD zhengguan · year_domain.Social: You take on roles among friends this year, a committee seat or a host's duty, and become known for showing up when you said you would.

units.GOD zhengyin · season_need.shown: What you get from the Sage on show is its element feeding and steadying you, the nourishment a season low in it holds back.
units.GOD zhengyin · seen.inside: Privately you want to be looked after and stay close to the people who once taught you.
units.GOD zhengyin · seen.plain: You look calm and well taught, someone a teacher or an older friend has clearly looked after.
units.GOD zhengyin · year_domain.Family: Your home draws a relative's closer interest this year, with help and opinions that leave you more looked after than you asked to be.
units.GOD zhengyin · year_domain.Health: This year you accept more looking after than you normally allow, leaning on shelter, quiet evenings and someone else's care.
units.GOD zhengyin · year_domain.Mind: You learn most this year when someone else sets the syllabus, with books, courses and a patient teacher filling your evenings.

units.POSITION bijian_month_stem · chapter.now: Your Rising Chapter is the one where you prove yourself alone. Since your late teens you have taken whole jobs and signed your name to them, and you trust what you carried yourself more than anything you were handed.
units.POSITION jiecai_hour_branch · chapter.co: Behind it, the people after you push against you and stand up for you in the same breath. You hold your own place in these years only where you fixed its size early.
units.POSITION piancai_day_branch · chapter.co: Your Home Chapter opens wider than the ones before it, through a partner whose world is bigger than yours. From your mid-thirties your days fill with new people, side ventures and offers you did not go looking for. You will say yes more often in this chapter than in any other, and most of those yeses pay you back.
units.POSITION piancai_day_branch · chapter.li: Your Home Chapter was the widest of your life, opened by a partner whose world was bigger than yours. Those years filled with new people, side ventures and offers you never went looking for. You said yes more often then than at any other time, and much of what you have now came through those doors.
units.POSITION piancai_day_branch · chapter.no: Your Home Chapter is wider than the ones before it, opened by a partner whose world is bigger than yours. Since your mid-thirties your days have filled with new people, side ventures and offers you did not go looking for. You say yes more often now than in any earlier chapter, and most of those yeses pay you back.
Beneath it runs a private education in things nobody asked you to learn. You are gathering the strange and specialist knowledge your later work is paid for, and you rarely explain it to anyone.
units.POSITION shishen_year_branch · chapter.l: Inside it ran a steady supply of comfort, good food and someone who made sure you were fed. You still trust that early ease, and you go back to it whenever life runs thin.
units.POSITION zhengcai_hour_stem · chapter.co: Your Late Chapter is the well-kept one, when the care of every earlier decade finally shows. From your late forties your days run on order and calm, and you are the person others call when something needs sorting out.
units.POSITION zhengcai_year_stem · chapter.li: Your Early Chapter was an orderly one, with money counted at home and promises kept in front of you. You came out of it careful, and the habits you formed then still run your accounts.
units.SEASON bing.chen · reading: Late spring warms you steadily while damp Earth gathers around you and dulls your glow. The season asks for river Water to carry your light and for Wood to break that Earth apart, and it keeps Metal well away from the Wood. You light up a whole valley once the soil has been broken open.
units.SEASON bing.chou · reading: Late winter gives your sun its nerve back, strong enough to laugh at the snow and melt the frost. This month looks to Water to carry that new strength, and with so much frozen Earth about it calls on Wood to break the ground. You outshine the last of the cold once the soil loosens.
units.SEASON bing.hai · reading: Early winter takes the sun out of season, with short days and cold water rising under you. The month wants Wood to keep your fire fed, Earth to hold back the water, and Metal to trim the Wood when it grows thick. You stay bright through the dark months by drawing on each of these as the weather changes.
units.SEASON bing.mao · reading: In mid-spring your warmth stretches out with ease, the sun riding higher over green fields. Everything this month comes down to Water, a river under your light kept full by Metal of every kind. You blaze at your fullest when no smaller fire draws that river away from you.
units.SEASON bing.shen · reading: Born in early autumn, you hang lower in the sky, and the light you give turns golden and slanting. This month wants Water beneath you most of all, broad river water that catches your glow and throws it back doubled. You look your brightest in that reflection, and you keep your shine as long as the water stays in measure.
units.SEASON bing.si · reading: Your birth falls in early summer, when you stand at full strength and the air shimmers with heat. The month calls on Water to take the edge off that blaze, a river that lets fire and water finish each other's work, with Metal at its source. You are at your most generous once a full river runs below you.
units.SEASON bing.wei · reading: Late summer is when your heat starts to ebb, fierce on the surface with the first coolness waiting beneath. Water is the main thing this season wants for you, a river steadied by Metal that keeps your light strong as it begins to soften. You stay brilliant into the turning weeks when no bank of Earth chokes that river.
units.SEASON bing.wu · reading: Midsummer is your peak, the sun at full height with heat pouring off it in every direction. Only a high and open river of Water can match you this month, and Metal behind it keeps that river from shrinking. You rise above ordinary days when nothing muddies the water or pulls it away.
units.SEASON bing.xu · reading: Late autumn draws your fire down further while heavy Earth piles up and dims what light remains. This season reaches first for Wood to break up that Earth and feed you, and second for Water, a river to restore your shine. You light up again when no blade cuts the Wood and no Earth buries the water.
units.SEASON bing.yin · reading: Early spring lifts you higher each day, the sun climbing as the year opens and your heat building with it. The month honours Water most, a broad river that reflects your light and keeps the warmth in measure, with Metal feeding that river from upstream. You shine clearest when no mountain of Earth stands between you and the world.
units.SEASON bing.you · reading: Mid-autumn brings you toward evening, your last light spread low across a lake. Water is what the season prizes for you, a river that holds your fading glow and keeps it in view. You keep that evening light longest when no hill of Earth gets in the way and no jewel of Metal pulls your gaze aside.
units.SEASON bing.zi · reading: Midwinter is where your light turns, the shortest day passing and your sun growing stronger from its lowest point. The season puts Water first, a river that gives the returning light a surface, with Earth beside it to hold the water in its banks. You gather strength through the cold months and come back brighter every week after the solstice.
units.SEASON ding.chen · reading: Late spring settles heavy Earth over your flame, damp soil that soaks up your warmth as fast as you make it. The month leans first on Wood to feed you and push that Earth back, then on Metal to split the Wood into pieces you can use. You find your light again once the fire has something dry to hold.
units.SEASON ding.chou · reading: At the end of winter your flame burns low under frozen ground, a candle in the last of the cold. This month prizes Wood most for fuel and Metal next to split it, while Earth and Water are used sparingly. You find your warmth again in the closing weeks of winter, once the wood is cut and dry.
units.SEASON ding.hai · reading: Early winter puts a slight chill on your flame as the nights draw in. The month honours Wood above all to keep you burning, with Metal as its partner to split the logs and Earth or Water brought in as the weather demands. You burn warmest through the cold when no soft Earth clings to the wood.
units.SEASON ding.mao · reading: In mid-spring damp vines crowd your flame, green growth that smokes more than it burns. This season wants Metal before all else to clear that wet growth away, and then Wood from a solid tree to give you dry fuel. You glow clean and clear once the smoke has gone and real timber is in reach.
units.SEASON ding.shen · reading: Born in early autumn, you are a soft flame drawing back while Metal rules the month without threatening you. The season calls for Wood as your fuel and Metal to cut it, with sunlight's Fire drying the wood first. You keep a steady glow into the cool weeks with dry kindling within reach.
units.SEASON ding.si · reading: You were born in early summer, when your flame rises to its full strength in the warm months. The season wants Wood for fuel and Metal to split it, the pairing that makes your fire burn clear instead of smoky. You give off your finest light in these weeks when no rain falls on you.
units.SEASON ding.wei · reading: Late summer weakens your flame more than the heat suggests, the first cool hiding inside the warm air. The month turns first to Wood to keep you burning and then to Water to steady you, with Metal on hand to split the fuel. You hold your light through the season's close when dry wood lies near.
units.SEASON ding.wu · reading: Midsummer brings your flame home to its strongest month, and more fuel only makes the heat harder to bear. The season looks instead to a river's Water to temper that fire and to Metal to keep the river fed, though a single clear rain also does the job. You rise above the crowd when no Earth dams that water.
units.SEASON ding.xu · reading: Late autumn surrounds your flame with dry Earth that drinks your warmth and gives little back. The season asks for Wood to keep you lit, and wherever there is Wood it wants Metal close by to split it. You turn sharp and articulate in this month, and you do your finest work once the fuel is cut and ready.
units.SEASON ding.yin · reading: Early spring piles fresh green Wood around your flame, more fuel than a small fire can catch. The month asks for Metal first to split that Wood into kindling, with a measure of Water to keep the blaze in check. You burn steady and bright when the fuel reaches you already cut.
units.SEASON ding.you · reading: Mid-autumn leaves your flame small against a cooling sky, a lamp burning while Metal fills the month. This month asks for Wood and Metal together, fuel and the blade that splits it, while the sun's Fire dries whatever you burn. Even dry grass lights you here, and you burn longest when the sun has warmed your fuel first.
units.SEASON ding.zi · reading: Midwinter rings your flame with cold water on every side, the darkest month for a small fire. The season looks to Wood as the one thing that keeps you alight and to Metal to split it, with Earth to bank the water when it rises. You hold your glow in the deep cold while dry wood stays beside you.
units.SEASON geng.chen · reading: You were born in late spring, when Earth runs the season and buries Metal more than it feeds it. Your season asks first for Wood to break that Earth open and then for Fire to temper you, and you come into your own when both are within reach.
units.SEASON geng.chou · reading: Late winter sinks you in cold wet mud, and the frost only deepens as the weeks go on. Fire from the sun comes first to thaw you, a working flame second to temper your Metal, and Wood alongside to feed them both. You thaw slowly, and you come out of the season sharper for the wait.
units.SEASON geng.hai · reading: Cold water surrounds you in early winter, and the chill settles into your Metal. The season asks for Fire twice over, a flame to shape you and the sun to warm you, with Wood to keep both burning. You warm to people and to work once that heat is steady.
units.SEASON geng.mao · reading: In mid-spring you are a blade among green branches, at your softest of the year. The season wants the Fire of a steady flame to forge you and Wood second to feed it, with Metal of your own kind splitting that Wood. You take shape under patient heat more than under force.
units.SEASON geng.shen · reading: Autumn opens in your own element, and it leaves you harder and keener than at any other time. What the season asks for is a forge, Fire to work you into shape and Wood behind it to keep the heat going. You do your finest work under that heat, and Water only dulls you here.
units.SEASON geng.si · reading: Metal first comes alive in early summer, and the heat around you warms more than it melts. A river's Water comes first to keep you cool and even, and solid Earth second to steady you with the sun beside it. You meet each problem with the answer it calls for, not with a fixed order.
units.SEASON geng.wei · reading: Late summer hides the first coolness of the year under its heat, and it leaves you blunt and stubborn. A working flame is the first thing it asks for, Fire to bring your edge back, and Wood second to keep that flame alive. You turn sharp again under steady heat, and people notice the change.
units.SEASON geng.wu · reading: Midsummer is the hardest month for a blade, with the year's fiercest Fire working on you until you soften. It asks only for Water, a river first and rain second, and you keep your edge through the heat once that cooling reaches you.
units.SEASON geng.xu · reading: Late autumn heaps Earth over you, and the risk is that it hides you completely. Wood comes first to dig that weight loose, and a river's Water second to rinse you clean, and you shine out once both have done their work.
units.SEASON geng.yin · reading: Early spring belongs to Wood, and winter's chill still clings to you while the Earth that feeds you sits too weak to help. The sun's Fire comes first to warm you, then Wood to stop Earth from piling over you, and you take your edge from heat more than from shelter.
units.SEASON geng.you · reading: The middle of autumn holds your edge at its keenest, and nothing about you has softened yet. It calls first for Fire as a forging flame with Wood to feed it, and then for the sun's wider warmth as well. You become useful rather than merely sharp once heat of both kinds surrounds you.
units.SEASON geng.zi · reading: The frost sets deep into you in midwinter, the coldest stretch of your year. The season still turns first to Fire as a small flame fed by Wood, and then to the sun to light and warm you. Your edge holds through the dark months once that fire is lit.
units.SEASON gui.chen · reading: Late spring warms you gently, pairing your rain with sunlight the way good weather does. The sun's Fire comes first to bring you into step with the season, and fine Metal and Wood follow to keep you fed as the heat climbs. You do best under a mild warmth, and it shows in how easily you work.
units.SEASON gui.chou · reading: Late winter is the coldest point of your year, and everything in you sets hard as ice. The sun's Fire is what breaks that freeze, a small flame helps keep the thaw going, and you loosen into your gentler self once the warmth arrives.
units.SEASON gui.hai · reading: Early winter looks like your strongest month, yet the first stirrings of new Wood drain you quietly from inside. Heavy and fine Metal together are what it asks for, to refill what that hidden growth takes from you. You stay strong all winter once your source is kept full.
units.SEASON gui.mao · reading: Mid-spring draws you out into every green thing that is growing, and you spend yourself faster than you refill. It asks for Metal above all, the heavy kind first and the fine kind second, to restore the source you keep pouring out. You hold your own once something is feeding you back.
units.SEASON gui.shen · reading: Hard Metal takes command in early autumn, and it feeds you more than you can use. Fire comes first as a steady flame to soften that Metal, and Wood second to keep the flame burning, and you turn all that support into something warm and usable.
units.SEASON gui.si · reading: The air heats around you in early summer, and a rain like you can dry out before it lands. Fine Metal is what the season wants first, a cool source that keeps you replenished, with heavier Metal as the second choice. You stay fresh through the hottest days with that source close by.
units.SEASON gui.wei · reading: Late summer dries you slowly, the heat easing while the ground stays thirsty for all you carry. Metal is the whole of what it asks, coarse and fine together, to keep your source from running dry. You stay generous through the late heat once that source is secure.
units.SEASON gui.wu · reading: You have almost nowhere to stand in midsummer, a thin rain falling into the fiercest heat of the year. The season asks for Metal of both kinds to give you a source, and for more Water beside you to guard that Metal from the heat. You get through this season once others like you stand with you.
units.SEASON gui.xu · reading: Late autumn presses hard on you, with heavy Earth in command and little to keep you flowing. Fine Metal comes first to reopen your source, then Wood to hold that Earth back, with more rain beside you to feed the Wood. You find your feet again once the pressure is shared out.
units.SEASON gui.yin · reading: Early spring makes you the softest of rains, quickly drawn into the new growth. The season asks first for fine Metal to keep your source flowing, and then for the sun's Fire to warm you, with heavier Metal as a further help. You give the most when you are refilled as fast as you give.
units.SEASON gui.you · reading: Mid-autumn pairs you with fine Metal, and you run as clear as water ever does. It wants that fine Metal first to keep you pure and fed, and the sun's Fire beside it to take off the chill. You are at your gentlest and clearest when both are near, warm water over bright stone.
units.SEASON gui.zi · reading: You come close to freezing in midwinter, rain turning to ice before it can fall. The season's first need is the sun's Fire to thaw you and keep you moving, and its second is fine Metal to hold your source open under the ice. You warm into yourself slowly, and you are worth the wait.
units.SEASON ji.chen · reading: Late spring is planting time, and your field is ready to take seed. Fire comes first to warm the ground and Water next to keep it moist, with Wood to break up the clods, and you yield a full crop once all three are close.
units.SEASON ji.chou · reading: Late winter leaves you wet and frozen at once, ice running through heavy soil. The season puts the sun's Fire first to thaw you out and keeps Wood beside it to feed that heat. What you planted in the dark wakes once the warmth breaks through, and you are ready for spring before most.
units.SEASON ji.hai · reading: Cold wet mud is what early winter makes of your field, with water rising over the low ground. Nothing grows in you until the sun's Fire comes to dry and warm that ground, and Wood comes second to keep the fire fed. You come back to life once that warmth holds.
units.SEASON ji.mao · reading: In the middle of spring the warmth in you is rising, and green shoots break your surface before the field has opened out. Wood comes first to loosen your soil and the Water of soft rain second to feed it, with the sun's Fire on top, and you flourish once the ground has been turned and watered.
units.SEASON ji.shen · reading: Early autumn draws strength out of you, the way a harvest takes from the field that grew it. Water comes first to moisten you and carry off the season's sharp Metal, and Fire second to warm you and keep that Metal in check, and you recover your spirit once both are close.
units.SEASON ji.si · reading: Your crops already stand in the field by early summer, and what they crave most is sweet rain. The season wants Water first to soak you and the sun's Fire second to ripen what grows, with a little Metal to keep the rain coming, and you prosper when neither heat nor rain runs short.
units.SEASON ji.wei · reading: Earth piles on Earth in late summer, and the heat sits heavy on your ground. Its first call is for Water to keep your soil soft enough to work, and its second is for Fire from the sun, with Metal standing behind the rain. You carry the most for others when you are kept both damp and warm.
units.SEASON ji.wu · reading: Midsummer bakes you dry, and your field cracks under the strongest heat of the year. This month wants Water before anything, rain to cool and soften you, and then the sun's Fire in measure to keep the crop growing. You stay generous through the hottest weeks once both are near.
units.SEASON ji.xu · reading: Late autumn packs you hard, with Earth heaped high in its own month. Its first need is Wood to break up that weight, then Water and Fire in turn to soften and warm what is left, and you turn fertile again once the clods are loosened.
units.SEASON ji.yin · reading: You were born in early spring, when your field is still frozen and the last of winter has not lifted. The season asks above all for the Fire of a full sun to thaw that ground and wake what is planted in it, and you start to grow the moment that warmth arrives.
units.SEASON ji.you · reading: The Metal season peaks in the middle of autumn, and it takes more out of your ground than any other month. Water returns first as rain to refill you and Fire follows to warm your strength back, with fine Metal feeding the rain, and you hold firm against the season with all three at your side.
units.SEASON ji.zi · reading: Midwinter freezes you solid, the field locked under the coldest weeks of the year. It asks for the sun's Fire before anything, the one warmth strong enough to thaw you, and for Wood as a second hand to keep that Fire burning. A candle does little for you here, and you loosen only under real sunlight.
units.SEASON jia.chen · reading: By late spring your growth has spent most of its push, and the ground turns heavy as Earth takes over. What this season asks for is Metal to carve you into something useful, then a river's Water to refill what spring used up. You stand tall again once blade and river both reach you.
units.SEASON jia.chou · reading: Winter's last month is the coldest stretch of your year, and your Wood sits frozen with no sign of growth. The season asks for Metal first to split you open and then for Fire to catch in the opened grain, the one it cannot do without. You shine in the deep cold the moment that flame takes hold.
units.SEASON jia.hai · reading: Early winter fills the ground with cold water, and a tree like you risks floating loose from its roots. The month wants Metal and Fire together, the blade to shape you and the flame to warm the blade, with Earth to bank the rising water. You stand firm through the first cold when the flood is held back.
units.SEASON jia.mao · reading: Mid-spring brings your Wood to full strength, a tree growing too fast to hold its shape. This month calls for Metal before anything else, a blade that prunes you into form, with Earth behind it to keep the blade supplied. You do your finest work under a firm hand, and too much rain dulls that edge.
units.SEASON jia.shen · reading: Born in early autumn, you arrive when Metal rules the month and timber is cut. The season honours Fire above all, a flame that works the blade into a tool, and it still wants the Metal to shape you. Rain puts the flame out, and you turn the cutting season into craft while the fire stays lit.
units.SEASON jia.si · reading: Your birth falls in early summer, when the sun takes charge and your sap starts to drain. The month turns to Water first, a rain that cools you, and to Fire second as a small flame that lets your growth be seen. You stay green through the long days when rain reaches you first.
units.SEASON jia.wei · reading: Late summer works on you quietly, the first cool hidden inside the heaviest heat. This season leans on Fire first to keep you warm and bright, then on Metal to give you edges, and takes rain only if it comes. You do well at summer's close when a small flame keeps burning beside you.
units.SEASON jia.wu · reading: Midsummer is the height of the heat, and your Wood dries out faster than it can drink. Water as rain matters most to keep you supple, with Fire as a steady flame next to let your talent shine and Metal last to trim you. You flourish in the hottest weeks once the rain comes first.
units.SEASON jia.xu · reading: Late autumn strips you bare, leaves falling and roots drying in a month ruled by Earth. The season loves Fire most to keep you lit, then Water as rain and river to feed what is left of your growth, with Metal and solid ground in support. You come through the bare months whole when warmth and water both stay near.
units.SEASON jia.yin · reading: You were born at the very start of spring, a young tree standing in frost that has not yet lifted. The season wants Fire first to warm you through and then Water as soft rain to feed your roots, and you grow fastest with your face turned to the sun.
units.SEASON jia.you · reading: Mid-autumn is when Metal stands strongest, and your Wood is held in its grip, cut back and cooling. Fire is wanted twice over, first as a close flame that softens that Metal and then as full sun to warm you. You hold your ground in this month once fire stands between you and the cold.
units.SEASON jia.zi · reading: In midwinter you are a tree in frozen ground, cold to the core while rain turns to ice around you. This season looks to Fire before anything to thaw you, then to Metal to give your shape an edge, with the sun lending a hand. You come alive in the dark months beside a fire that stays lit.
units.SEASON ren.chen · reading: Late spring heaps Earth against you, and too much of it silts up your course. Wood comes first to break that Earth apart and Metal second to keep your source running, and you move freely again once the silt is cleared.
units.SEASON ren.chou · reading: Late winter freezes you at the edges, though a thaw is closer than it looks. The sun's Fire comes first to loosen you, with a smaller flame and some Wood to keep that warmth going. You start to flow again the moment the ice gives way, and you move quickly once you do.
units.SEASON ren.hai · reading: Your own season arrives in early winter, and you run at full strength with nothing in your way. Earth comes first as a high bank to hold that force, and sunlight second to warm it, with Metal guarding that bank from roots that would loosen it. You are most useful when your strength has clear edges.
units.SEASON ren.mao · reading: In the middle of spring the cold has left you, and your streams run together into one wide flow. It needs no extra warmth now, only Earth first to give that flow its banks and fine Metal second to feed it from the source. You go furthest when something firm holds your course.
units.SEASON ren.shen · reading: Early autumn opens a deep source under you, and you swell from weak to strong. The season wants Earth first to give all that water its banks, and Fire second as a steady flame to back the Earth and check the Metal that feeds you. You do your best work once your force has a firm course.
units.SEASON ren.si · reading: Your water runs lowest in early summer, a river shrinking under a hot sun. What helps first is more Water of your own kind beside you, then fine Metal to restart your source, with heavier Metal behind it. You find your strength again through people like you more than through effort alone.
units.SEASON ren.wei · reading: The ground thickens around you in late summer, and though the heat is fading your banks are clogged. Fine Metal comes first to feed your source and Wood second to cut through the heavy Earth, with rain to top you up. You run clear again once the channel has been opened.
units.SEASON ren.wu · reading: Midsummer is the driest month for you, with the strongest heat of the year drawing your water down. Water comes first as rain to cool that heat and join your flow, and Metal second to open a fresh spring beneath you. You keep moving through the heat once both are with you.
units.SEASON ren.xu · reading: Late autumn walls you in with Earth, and your flow slows behind the dam. Wood comes first to work that Earth loose and give you an outlet, and the warmth of the sun's Fire follows to stir what has gone still. You move again once both are present, and the stillness turns into purpose.
units.SEASON ren.yin · reading: Early spring sets you running wide, but the new growth drinks from you and leaves you thinner than you look. The season asks first for Metal at your source to keep you fed, and then for the sun's Fire to warm the flow, and you carry far once that source is secure.
units.SEASON ren.you · reading: The middle of autumn leaves you clear and clean, Water fed by bright Metal at its purest. It asks for Wood above all, an outlet that turns all that clarity into growth, with heavier Metal as a second help. You give the most when your clarity has somewhere to go.
units.SEASON ren.zi · reading: Deep and cold, you grow stronger still in midwinter and harder to contain than in any other month. The month wants solid Earth first to give you a course and Fire from the sun beside it to keep you from freezing over, and you carry great weight once both stand around you.
units.SEASON wu.chen · reading: Late spring is your own month, with Earth in charge and your mountain grown thick and heavy. The season reaches for Wood first to break that weight apart, then for Fire to warm what has been opened, and for Water after that. You feel lighter and more useful when roots are working their way through you.
units.SEASON wu.chou · reading: Late winter keeps your mountain frozen through, wet ground locked hard under old snow. Sunlight is the one thing this month asks for, Fire with Wood behind it feeding that warmth. You soften and open as the year turns, and you start to give again once the thaw reaches you.
units.SEASON wu.hai · reading: Early winter brings your mountain a brief warm spell before the real cold, a little summer at the start of the dark months. The month wants Wood first to keep your soil alive and Fire second to keep it warm. You make the most of the mild days, and you stay green when no Metal cuts the Wood away.
units.SEASON wu.mao · reading: In mid-spring green growth climbs your slopes while the stone beneath still holds some cold. The sun's Fire comes before anything to warm you, with Wood next to loosen the soil and Water last of all to feed it. You turn from bare rock into a hill people want to walk on once that warmth comes through.
units.SEASON wu.shen · reading: Born in early autumn, you feel the warmth sink into your ground while the first cold rises out of it. The month asks for Fire first to keep your stone warm and for Water second to keep the soil soft, with Wood lending a hand. You stay fertile into the cooler weeks when the light holds on your slopes.
units.SEASON wu.si · reading: You were born in early summer, solid on the outside and hollow within, warm on the surface and cool at the core. Wood is what the month needs most to open you up and set things growing, with Fire and Water in support. You come alive under the heat once something takes root in you.
units.SEASON wu.wei · reading: Late summer leaves your mountain parched, dust on the slopes and every spring run low. Water as rain is the first thing this month wants for you, with Fire and Wood after it to keep the ground warm and broken open. You turn green again when the water comes first and the rest follows.
units.SEASON wu.wu · reading: Midsummer bakes your mountain dry, the stone hot to the touch and the soil cracking. The season looks first to a river's Water to cool and soak the ground, then to Wood to keep it loose and green. A light rain does little at this heat, and you are at your best once real water runs across your slopes.
units.SEASON wu.xu · reading: Late autumn piles your mountain high and dry, with Earth at full power and little else moving on it. Sunlight alone is not enough this month, which looks first to Wood to break the mass apart and then to Water to soften what the Wood has opened. You feel useful and alive once something grows through the hard ground.
units.SEASON wu.yin · reading: Early spring leaves your mountain cold and bare, with the thaw only starting on its slopes. The season wants Fire first as sunlight to warm the ground, then Wood to break the soil and bring it to life, and Water after that to make anything grow. You become a living hillside when all three reach you in that order.
units.SEASON wu.you · reading: Mid-autumn draws Metal out of your mountain and leaves the rock colder and thinner than before. The season relies on Fire to warm you back and on Water to keep the ground soft, and it can do without Wood. You give generously in these months, and you keep your strength when the sun stays on you.
units.SEASON wu.zi · reading: In midwinter your mountain freezes solid, ice in every crevice and snow across the summit. The season depends on Fire alone to thaw you, with Wood as its helper to keep that fire supplied. You warm slowly and hold heat a long time, and you thaw the moment the light reaches your slopes.
units.SEASON xin.chen · reading: Late spring gives you plenty of support, with Earth in charge of the season and feeding you generously. Water from a river comes first to keep you bright and Wood second to thin out the Earth, and you shine brightest when the help around you leaves you free.
units.SEASON xin.chou · reading: Late winter is the deepest freeze of your year, and you lie locked in ice and damp ground. The sun's Fire has to come first to thaw you and running Water second to wash off what the winter left, with Earth as a later help. You come out polished only after you have been warmed and rinsed.
units.SEASON xin.hai · reading: Early winter opens with a short false spring before the cold comes down on you. It asks first for flowing Water to keep you washed and bright, and then for the sun's Fire to warm you as the days shorten. You glint at your best in that brief warmth, and you carry the shine into the cold.
units.SEASON xin.mao · reading: Spring at its midpoint is mild and kind to you, and the only threat is Earth that clouds your shine. It honours running Water above all to wash you, and then Wood to hold back the Earth that would muddy that water. Kept clean and uncovered, you are noticed without having to ask.
units.SEASON xin.shen · reading: A jewel in its own season, you are whole and strong in early autumn with little to fear. A modest stream is all the season asks, Water enough to wash you without flooding you, with a touch of Wood and Earth as the moment calls. You shine with very little help in this month, and you know it.
units.SEASON xin.si · reading: Early summer brings a dry fierce heat that dulls your shine. The season wants a river's Water above all to rinse and cool you, then Wood to keep Earth from piling up, and rain as a lighter help. You are clear right through once the washing reaches you, and people trust what they see.
units.SEASON xin.wei · reading: Late summer smothers you with help, Earth so thick around you that your light is hidden. Its first call is for running Water to uncover and wash you, and its second for heavier Metal to keep that water flowing. You are seen for what you are once the extra cover is cleared away.
units.SEASON xin.wu · reading: You are at your most delicate in midsummer, far too soft for the forging that the month's heat offers. The month asks for cool flowing Water and soft sheltering Earth together, with rain as a smaller stand-in for the river. You keep your polish through the hottest weeks when that cool and that shelter stay close.
units.SEASON xin.xu · reading: Late autumn piles Earth around you and swells you with more strength than you can use. Water comes first as a clean current to carry off that excess, and Wood after it to loosen the Earth, while Fire and more Earth only add to the weight. You turn clear and light again once that work is done.
units.SEASON xin.yin · reading: Early spring hands the year to Wood, and a jewel like you has little strength of its own. The season asks first for soft Earth to feed and hold you, then for a river's Water to bring out your shine, with heavier Metal in support. You show your worth once you are both held and washed.
units.SEASON xin.you · reading: Mid-autumn brings you to the peak of your strength, and more support at this point only weighs you down. The season wants one thing, a river's Water to wash and channel all that force, with Wood only where Earth gathers too thick. You come out bright and quick once the excess runs off.
units.SEASON xin.zi · reading: Freezing rain frosts you over in midwinter and hides the sun. The month's first need is Water in full flow to keep you clean and moving, and its second the sun's Fire, with Earth and Wood steadying both. You glitter in the cold once those two are close beside you.
units.SEASON yi.chen · reading: By late spring the heat is climbing faster than the soil can hold water, and your vine begins to thirst. This month reaches for Water first to keep you supple and for Fire second to bring you into bloom. You come into full flower when loose Earth and hard Metal both keep their distance.
units.SEASON yi.chou · reading: Late winter keeps you in a cold valley, a vine waiting under frost for the year to turn. The season asks for one thing only, Fire as a clear sun that brings spring back early to the valley floor. You flower before the rest of the year when that light reaches you clear of any rain.
units.SEASON yi.hai · reading: Early winter brings cold water up around your roots, more than a vine can take in, and growth stops. The month turns to Fire first to warm you and then to Earth as solid ground to hold back the water and give you footing. You stay above the flood when warmth and firm ground reach you together.
units.SEASON yi.mao · reading: Mid-spring warms you without effort, the vine in full leaf and the cold behind you. The season crowns Fire as the sun you reach for and keeps Water as its helper, one to open your flowers and the other to keep them fed. You spread widest when no Metal is cutting at your roots.
units.SEASON yi.shen · reading: Born in early autumn, you feel the colder air as Metal takes charge of the month. The season wants Fire first to soften that Metal and keep you warm, then Water to keep your leaves from drying, and soft Earth to hold your roots. You stay rooted through the turning season when that ground is under you.
units.SEASON yi.si · reading: Early summer already gives you more sun than you asked for, and your vine starts to wilt through the long bright days. What you need now is Water above everything else, with Metal standing behind it as the source that keeps the rain coming. You stay fresh through the heat as long as that rain does not run dry.
units.SEASON yi.wei · reading: Late summer dries the ground around you and hides the first cool of autumn under the heat. Water does the main work this month, soaking your roots, while Fire keeps you warm as that cool creeps in and Metal feeds the water from behind. You thrive at the end of summer once heavy Earth stays out of the way.
units.SEASON yi.wu · reading: Your birth falls in midsummer, when fire runs the month and the fields lie parched. Water is wanted first and most to save your leaves, and Fire joins it as sunlight once the dog days bring their hidden chill. You green again after one good soaking, and you carry that freshness into the cooler months.
units.SEASON yi.xu · reading: Late autumn dries your roots and drops your leaves, leaving the vine bare in hard ground. Everything this season turns on Water to bring you back to life, with fine Metal upstream to keep the rain flowing. Strong sun only bakes the ground harder, and you recover when the water reaches you first.
units.SEASON yi.yin · reading: You arrive at the start of spring, a young vine in air that still holds the winter's chill. This month puts Fire first, a sun that warms you as nothing else can, and lets Water follow as rain once the cold eases. You climb toward any warmth, and you grow quickly when the sun comes before the rain.
units.SEASON yi.you · reading: Mid-autumn is your flowering season, the vine that blooms when everything else is fading. Before the flowers open you want Water to feed the buds, and once they open you turn toward Fire as sunlight with rain close behind. You blossom late and well, and you are at your best when people least expect a bloom.
units.SEASON yi.zi · reading: In midwinter your vine freezes where it stands, though the light has already begun its slow return. This season leans on Fire alone, a sun to thaw you and turn your face toward the coming spring. Rain only adds to the frost, and you start to grow again the moment the sun touches you.
units.STAR guchen · line: You need more time alone inside closeness than most.
units.STAR guchen · reading.day.coming: From your mid-thirties you need stretches of solitude even inside the closest relationship of your life. A partner will read it as distance more than once, and you stay longest with the person who lets you go quiet without asking why.
units.STAR hongluan · reading.month.now: Your Rising Chapter carries more attraction than you planned for, much of it through work and study and the circles those years bring. You have been noticed more than you noticed, and you kept at least one feeling from these years to yourself.
units.STAR jiesha · line: Loss taught you to guard what is yours.
units.STAR jiesha · reading.year.lived: Something in your first home could be taken without warning, a place of your own or a promise or a plan. You learned to guard what was yours younger than most, and you still move faster than others when something of yours is at risk.
units.STAR kongwang · arriving.year: Some of what you push for this year stays empty for a while, an answer that does not come or a plan that waits. You lose less than it seems, and you use what you held back once the year turns.
units.STAR taohua · arriving.decade.coming: In this decade your life fills with new people, more invitations and more attention than you have had before. You enjoy it more openly than you expect, and you choose the few who stay with care.
units.STAR taohua · line.arriving: This decade brings new people in numbers.
units.STAR tianyi · arriving.decade.now: Someone with standing opens a door for you in this decade, a mentor or a sponsor who backs you before you have proved yourself. The help arrives while you are already working hard, and it costs you nothing to accept.
units.STAR tianyi · arriving.year: This year the help is close enough to name, an introduction or a recommendation from someone above you. You get further on it than on a year of effort, and you remember who gave it.
units.STAR tianyi · line.arriving: A helper with standing arrives in this decade.
units.STAR wangshen · line: You keep part of yourself out of sight.
units.STAR wangshen · reading.day.coming: From your mid-thirties you keep a part of your life out of sight, plans and feelings that even a partner hears about late. It protects you more than it costs you, and you choose carefully who gets to see all of you.
units.STAR wenchang · line: Words and learning come easily to you.
units.STAR wenchang · reading.year.lived: You learned to read early and took to schoolwork faster than your effort explains. Written work and anything you could study for went better for you than for most, and you still trust a book to get you through a hard problem.
units.STAR yangren · reading.hour.coming: From your late forties a will rises in you that does not bend, and you keep it for the moments that matter. You defend what you have built firmly enough that people step back, and you keep the peace by choosing which fights are worth having.
units.STRUCTURE jianlu_ge · reading: Your chart takes its shape from your own strength, with little handed down and most things built by hand. You do best where effort is paid to you directly. You are proudest of what you made with nobody's help.
units.STRUCTURE officer · status.broken.unchec: The General bears down with nothing to check it, and more is asked of you than you can carry alone. You get through on the allies beside you, and each hard stretch leaves you tougher.
units.STRUCTURE officer · status.broken.virtuo: The Virtuoso talks back to the Magistrate unchecked, and you lose roles over what you say to the people above you. You come through on work judged by results more than rank.
units.STRUCTURE officer · status.formed.none: Duty and pressure work in your favour, and the demands placed on you come with standing attached. You stand on your title and your word, and you carry heavy roles without losing your footing.
units.STRUCTURE officer · status.strained.gene: The General stands beside your Magistrate, and you answer to two bosses with different rules. You spend effort working out whose terms apply, and your record looks less settled than your work deserves.
units.STRUCTURE officer · status.strained.mixe: The Magistrate sits beside your General, and you switch between fighting for ground and asking for it politely. People above you get mixed signals, and you lose credit that one clear approach would win.
units.STRUCTURE officer · status.strained.unch: Nothing in your chart softens the General, and every demand reaches you at full force. You bear it, and you pay in rest and goodwill for meeting each fight head on.
units.STRUCTURE output · status.broken.alchemi: The Alchemist crowds out the Artisan, and what you mean to make stays unmade while you study it. You come through on what you learn meanwhile, and it becomes work only a specialist can do.
units.STRUCTURE output · status.broken.magistr: The Magistrate stands over your Virtuoso, and every rule you work under becomes a quarrel. You get through on talent people pay for in its own right, outside the chain of command.
units.STRUCTURE output · status.formed.none: What you make and say reaches people without getting stuck on the way. Your talent opens doors for you, and the work you enjoy keeps finding someone who wants it.
units.STRUCTURE piancai_ge · reading: Your chart runs on range, money that moves and openings that arrive through side doors. You do best with several things in play at once, a deal here and a contact there. You earn most where you are free to roam.
units.STRUCTURE pianyin_ge · reading: At the centre of your chart sits private study, the unusual knowledge few people around you share. You are at your best in a niche of your own, on a problem nobody else can read. You rely on what you worked out more than on what you were taught.
units.STRUCTURE qisha_ge · reading: Your chart answers to pressure, the hard test and the person who pushes back. You rise when the risk is real and the deadline is close. In the thick of a fight, you are at your steadiest.
units.STRUCTURE seal · status.formed.none: Learning and shelter hold steady around you, from teachers, credentials and people who vouch for you. What you know keeps you safe, and you recover from a setback faster than the people around you.
units.STRUCTURE seal · status.strained.money: Money pulls at your learning, and study keeps losing out to whatever pays this month. You trade courses and mentors for earnings, and the shelter behind you wears thinner each time.
units.STRUCTURE seal · status.strained.starved: The Alchemist leaves the Artisan little to eat, and you lose finished work and easy pleasures to second thoughts. You know far more than you have shown anyone.
units.STRUCTURE self · status.formed.none: Your own strength carries you, and you finish what you start without waiting for help. You can lean on your nerve and your circle of equals, and you stand firm when others wobble.
units.STRUCTURE self · status.strained.idle: Your strength has nothing to work on, no task or prize or person to answer to. You spend it on restless plans and contests with friends, and you get back less than you put in.
units.STRUCTURE shangguan_ge · reading: Your chart turns on a sharp voice and a talent that refuses to sit quietly. You shine where you are judged on what you can do, on a stage or under your own name. When nobody stands over you, you do your finest work.
units.STRUCTURE shishen_ge · reading: Your chart grows out of ease and appetite, the pleasure of making something well and sharing it. You thrive at your own pace on work you enjoy. What you make with a light hand is what people come back for.
units.STRUCTURE wealth · status.broken.peers: Equals reach your money with nothing to stop them, and what you earn leaves through friends, partners and shared plans. You come through because you earn it back faster than it goes.
units.STRUCTURE wealth · status.formed.none: What you earn arrives on time and stays long enough to build on. You can count on a steady return from your work, and you keep hold of it without a fight.
units.STRUCTURE wealth · status.formed.peers: Equals stand close to your money, and a rule or contract keeps each share in place. You can lean on clear terms with friends and partners, and you come out with your part intact.
units.STRUCTURE wealth · status.strained.none: Money and the duties that come with it arrive faster than you can hold them. You work hard for gains that slip away, and you tire of the upkeep before you enjoy the reward.
units.STRUCTURE wealth · status.strained.peers: The {breakers} {stand} close to your {gods}, and you keep losing a share of what you earn to equals.
units.STRUCTURE yuejie_ge · reading: Your chart centres on the Rival, on equals who compete with you and share in whatever you have. You work hardest in a team where everyone can see the score. You win more in an open contest than in a quiet deal.
units.STRUCTURE yueren_ge · reading: Everything in your chart gathers around the Rival, a hard and competitive will that does not back down. You do best against a real opponent or under strict discipline, and that edge earns its keep when you have something to guard.
units.STRUCTURE zhengcai_ge · reading: Your chart is built around money kept and value earned. You do best when the work in front of you has a clear return, and you trust a slow sure gain over a fast one.
units.STRUCTURE zhengguan_ge · reading: Your chart is built around duty kept and a role held in public. You do best inside a clear order, with a title and terms written down. You keep your word long after others have bent theirs.
units.STRUCTURE zhengyin_ge · reading: Your chart rests on shelter and learning, on teachers who back you and places that look after their own. You do your best work where study is valued and someone senior vouches for you. You repay that care with years of loyalty.

units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.bind.month_da: Your job and your home draw on the same circle of people, a partner met through work or your parents' friends, and the line between them stays thin.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.bind.month_ho: You carry the people and skills of your working life into your later years, keeping close the circle you build at work.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.bind.year_day: You build your own home close to the habits of the one you grew up in, and you return to them more than you expected.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.bind.year_hou: You pass the customs of your first family to the young people you raise or train, until your later years echo your earliest ones.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.bind.year_mon: Your first family stays tied to your working life, with a trade or a contact or a loyalty from home going into every job you hold.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.clash.day_hou: The people after you pull against the life you share with a partner, but you keep both by moving house or reworking your days.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.clash.month_d: Your work and your home compete for the same hours, and a new job or a new address follows whenever the strain grows too loud.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.clash.month_h: What you build at work in your rising years stops fitting your later life, and you change course when that chapter opens rather than hold on to it.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.clash.year_da: You make a household that breaks sharply from the home of your childhood, keeping a partner and your first family at a careful distance.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.clash.year_ho: You raise or train the people after you by rules you wrote yourself, because little from the house you grew up in passes to them cleanly.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.clash.year_mo: Your choice of work breaks with what your family expected, and you make your own way in a trade nobody at home chose.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.frame.day_hou: You, a partner and the young ones you raise or train pull together around one shared aim, your household growing stronger with each passing year.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.frame.month_d: Your work feeds straight into your household, with you and a partner backing the same plan or running something together.
Work, home and the people after you build on each other, and you keep growing what you start in your rising years through every later decade.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.frame.month_h: You carry the momentum of your work well into later life, counting the people you train along the way among your strongest allies.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.frame.year_da: Your first family stands behind the home you make, keeping their help close at hand while you build a household with a partner.
You bring your first family and the people who follow you together, making your own home the place where three generations meet.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.frame.year_ho: You pass something your first family began to the young ones after you, adding to it alongside them through your later years.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.frame.year_mo: Your working life starts at a run from the household you grew up in, through doors your parents or siblings open for you.
Your first family, your work and your own home all serve one aim, and it gathers force as you carry it from stage to stage.
You watch one story gather weight across every part of your life, from your first home through work and partnership to the people after you.
You carry skills learned in your first home through your career into the people you train, becoming the link that passes them forward.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.harm.day_hour: You spend years smoothing over a quiet friction between a partner and the younger ones in your life, the complaints nobody says out loud.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.harm.month_da: Late evenings and calls on days off wear quietly at your home life, and you guard one part of every week from your work.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.harm.month_ho: Your work rubs at the people after you in small ways, a missed evening or a forgotten promise that you make up to them in person.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.harm.year_day: You settle an old irritation from your first home one small argument at a time, after it follows you into your life with a partner.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.harm.year_hou: You notice a tone or a rule from your childhood rubbing at how you treat the children you raise or train, and smooth it over before it grows.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.harm.year_mon: Your family never quite approves of the work you choose, a quiet doubt you answer with results more than with arguments.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.none_hard: You move from one chapter of your life to the next without a sharp break, because no clash, punishment or harm sits between your gates.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.punish.day_ho: The same argument returns at home between you and those who follow you, but you break the loop by changing your own rule first.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.punish.month_: You bring the standards of your work home, holding a partner to the demands you make of colleagues until you draw a line where the job stops.
You pass the pressure you put on yourself at work to the people you train, easing it once you see them repeat your hardest years.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.punish.year_d: You hear old house rules from your childhood in your own voice with a partner, and rewrite them one at a time as they come back.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.punish.year_h: You hold the people after you to the standards you were raised on, with the same friction repeating until you decide which of those rules to keep.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.punish.year_m: Your family's expectations follow you into every job, driving you harder than any boss asks until you settle on your own measure.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.selfpunish.da: What you struggle with at home reappears in the people after you, and breaking the habit in yourself first keeps them from inheriting it.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.selfpunish.mo: You make the same mistake at work and at home, taking on too much and resenting it later, catching it sooner each time it returns.
You meet a habit that holds you back at work a second time in your later life, seeing it coming early and turning it down.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · bond.selfpunish.ye: The quarrel you grew up around repeats in your own home with a partner, and you end it by changing your own part in it.
Your childhood plays out again around the young ones in your care, and the old scene gets a different ending once you recognise it early.
You play the role you had in your family again at work, the peacemaker or the one who carries everything, and change it once you see it twice.

units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · structure_rule.non: Nothing hidden in your strongest seat shows on your stems. The {god} who holds it is the organising force of your life, and you answer to it first.

units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · structure_rule.ren: Your strongest seat holds your own element at its sharpest. Your chart is built around your own will, and you answer first to what you decide.
units.TEMPLATED tpl_depth · structure_rule.res: A trace of {element} deep in your strongest seat shows on {count} of your stems. That makes the {god} the organising force of your life, and you answer to it more than to the {holder} who holds the seat.
